chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What has Allah prescribed in the prayer?' He said, 'The time, the purification, the bowing, the prostration, the direction of prayer, the supplication, and the orientation.' I said, 'And what is besides that?' He said, 'It is a sunnah within the obligatory act.'
ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory and recommended components of Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the six fundamental pillars of prayer—time, purity, postures, direction, supplication, and orientation—establishing the baseline for validity. It provides crucial jurisprudential clarity by categorizing all other ritual elements as *sunnah*, thereby distinguishing between the mandatory core and the recommended enhancements that perfect the prayer.
